prompt: Write the body (about 120 words) of a letter of representation from a personal injury lawyer to an auto insurer. The client was hurt in a parking lot collision. Ask that all contact go through the law firm, ask for the policy limits, and ask the insurer to keep all evidence. No salutation, no signature, no names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1208; do not mention it.)
text:
This firm represents our client in connection with a collision that occurred in a parking lot and resulted in significant personal injuries to our client. Please direct all further communication regarding this matter to our office and do not contact our client directly, whether by telephone, mail, or in person. If your insured or any representative of your company has already spoken with our client, please note that we expect all future contact to pass through this firm.

We request that you provide the bodily injury liability limits under the policy issued to your insured, together with a certified copy of the declarations page and any applicable umbrella or excess coverage that may apply. Please confirm in writing within fourteen days of receiving this letter.

We also ask that your company preserve all evidence relating to this incident. This includes photographs, dash camera or surveillance footage, vehicle data, adjuster notes, recorded statements, repair estimates, and any other documents or electronic records in your possession or control. Destroying or altering any of this material could expose your company to serious legal consequences.

We look forward to your prompt response.
